Strongest El Nino in 40 years threatens global weather disruption
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:18:00 UTC
16:18:00 KST

El Nino is forecast to become the strongest in four decades of comparable records, the United Nations' weather agency warned Thursday, as the U.N. chief said the world was entering the "danger zone of extreme weather."
The weather phenomenon is expected to strengthen to "very strong" levels in the coming months and is almost certain to persist through February, the World Meteorological Organization said.
"If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began," WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva.
El Nino is expected to peak toward the end of this year, but its effects on global weather and climate could persist well into 2027, the WMO said.
The phenomenon occurs when surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, triggering widespread changes in atmospheric circulation, winds, pressure and rainfall patterns around the world.
Heat in the oceans is released more slowly into the atmosphere, pushing up global temperatures the year after El Nino develops.
The powerful 2023-24 El Nino contributed to 2024 being the warmest year on record, and "we should not be surprised if this record is broken," Saulo added.
"El Nino is firmly established and will intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with big impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat," the WMO said.
El Nino is a naturally occurring phenomenon and is not caused by climate change.
But scientists expect it to exacerbate the heat of a planet already warming because of the burning of fossil fuels, while amplifying weather extremes.
"El Nino is being supersized before our eyes," said U.N. chief Antonio Guterres.
"The science leaves no room for doubt: The planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up. Sea surface temperatures are rising, temperatures keep climbing, and the world is in the danger zone of extreme weather."
WMO chief Saulo urged disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors such as agriculture, fisheries, health, energy and water to prepare.
"This exceptional El Nino ... has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world," she said.
"We are already seeing disruption and devastation from droughts and floods, and we expect these impacts to increase as El Nino intensifies."
El Nino typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts about nine to 12 months.
Conditions oscillate between El Nino and its opposite, La Nina, with neutral conditions in between.
El Nino can reshape weather and climate patterns thousands of kilometers away from the tropical Pacific.
Wilfran Moufouma-Okia, the WMO's climate prediction chief, said some places would be affected before, some during and some after the peak later this year, though the strength of the peak is not an indicator of the severity of the impacts.
For September-November, WMO forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of above-normal temperatures "across almost all land areas."
The index that measures sea surface temperature anomalies in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific has strengthened from an average of 1.5 degrees Celsius above normal between May and July.
Weekly values between late July and mid-August ranged from about 2.2 to 2.6 degrees Celsius above average, indicating continued El Nino intensification.
The U.N. agency classifies El Nino events as weak, moderate, strong or very strong, meaning this one is set to reach the highest level of the four categories.
Moufouma-Okia said the classification meant a sea surface temperature anomaly of more than 2 degrees Celsius.
"That category is open: We know where it starts; we don't know where it ends," he told Agence France-Presse (AFP).
The average forecast points toward an anomaly peaking at 3.6 degrees Celsius, far higher than the last two very strong El Nino events in 1997-98 and 2015-16.
In some areas, subsurface ocean temperatures were more than 8 degrees Celsius above average during July and early August.
Saulo called this a huge reservoir of "very warm ocean waters that will fuel the intensity of El Nino."
The U.N.'s International Organization for Migration appealed Thursday for $110 million to protect 4.9 million people from the potentially severe impacts of the phenomenon.

====================================================================================================

Taiwan-developed automated repositioning mattress cuts nursing workload by 69%
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:12:40 UTC
16:12:40 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Wellell Inc.’s automated repositioning mattress has entered clinical use at National Taiwan University Hospital after a joint study found that it reduced the workload required to reposition patients by 69%, CTEE reported.
In intensive care units, many critically ill patients need help repositioning every two to three hours. The task can be difficult when they are connected to multiple tubes and life-support equipment, often requiring two or three staff members, NTUH Department of Nursing’s Hsiao Wei-ling (蕭偉伶) said.
Frequent repositioning helps prevent pressure injuries in patients but can also increase the risk of lower back, shoulder, and neck injuries among nursing staff. The system was developed based on the needs of frontline clinicians and underwent multiple rounds of design improvements before clinical testing.
The study involved 424 critically ill patients and found that the mattress reduced overall nursing repositioning workloads by 69%. It cut the time required for each procedure by 53%, while the proportion of procedures that could be completed by a single nurse increased from 36.7% to 91.8%.
The findings suggest that the technology can not only ease the physical burden on nursing staff but also help protect critically ill patients from pressure injuries. The rate of new pressure injuries fell from 4.7% among patients who received conventional manual repositioning to 2.9% among those using the automated system.
Wellell announced Wednesday that it had donated 20 automated repositioning mattresses to NTUH, marking their introduction into the hospital’s intensive care units. NTUH Superintendent Yu Chong-jen (余忠仁) said similar equipment is already available overseas, but such products are expensive and may not fully suit Taiwan’s clinical needs.
Wellell said the system can adjust its repositioning angle, inflation level, and speed according to each patient’s weight and condition. Each procedure takes five to 10 minutes, or up to 15 minutes at the slowest setting. The company said gradual movement helps prevent patients from shifting or tubes from becoming dislodged.

Reform UK has suspended two senior officials after they were filmed in an undercover investigation appearing to plot to get around electoral laws on foreign donations.

Jukes and Orr were filmed by a group of investigative journalists called Verbatim, founded by the Centre for Climate Reporting, helping to orchestrate a plot apparently to bypass election laws.
The journalists posed as a potential Reform supporter and his wealthy American father, an impermissible donor, who paid for £30,000 of polling commissioned by Reform and which benefited the party when it was published in national newspapers.
If found to have been a donation in kind and made from abroad, it would have been impermissible as it was a foreign source and was not registered with the Electoral Commission.
Farage was subsequently caught on camera in a meeting with the fake US donor in Clacton where he appears to be celebrating the success of the poll, saying it was “amazing” and provided “bang for buck”. He said: “It worked. Boom.”
The Liberal Democrats and Labour have reported the actions of Reform to the police to investigate whether there has been a breach of electoral law.
The Electoral Commission, the watchdog that oversees the rules around party donations, said it had been in touch with the Metropolitan police and was “considering all relevant information”.
On Friday morning, Farage said the party had done nothing wrong and no rules were broken, saying on LBC that polls were funded by foreign sources all the time.
However, a Reform spokesperson said the officials would be suspended pending an investigation, saying: “Reform UK has launched an investigation following the broadcast of a Channel 4 News programme. Both individuals involved have stepped down from their respective positions pending the outcome of the investigation.
“The party believes it is important that the investigation is allowed to proceed independently and without prejudice. No further comment will be made while the investigation is ongoing.”
An Electoral Commission spokesperson said: “We are considering all relevant information, in line with our regulatory remit, and we are in touch with the Met police.”
They said any potential attempt to evade controls on donations was for the police to consider.
They also said they were not responsible for approving Reform UK’s or any other party’s donor vetting process, after Farage’s party said it had a “robust vetting process for prospective donors approved by the Electoral Commission”.
Reform initially described the investigation as a “hoax” and dismissed those behind it as activists, in a series of counterattacks against the outfit behind the undercover filming. But by Friday morning, it had taken action, as the statement announced the investigation into Orr and Jukes, in what appeared to be an attempt to distance Farage from their actions.
However, there appeared to be some controversy over how to deal with Orr and Jukes. Lee Anderson, the party’s chair, said they were not coming back, telling Sky News: “I think it’s only right and proper that we’re fair, open and transparent and get this investigation launched today. And the two people concerned in the video, they’ve gone.
“There’s no chance of them coming back. They’ve stepped aside. We’re a serious party, you know, and sometimes in politics, you have to make tough decisions, harsh decisions. I think this probably was an easier decision, being given the option to stand down. They have gone.”
But Richard Tice, the deputy leader, later did not rule out them returning to their roles after the inquiry. He also told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme the party had a legal opinion from a KC saying no rules had been broken and he believed Channel 4 News had broken rules with entrapment.
Asked by the Guardian at a fringe event at the Reform conference whether the pair had, as set out by Anderson, gone for good or might return the future, Danny Kruger, the MP who leads Reform’s preparations for government, indicated it was the latter. He said: “My understanding is that they have been suspended pending an investigation.”
The footage is likely to continue to raise awkward questions for Farage, on the day of his conference speech, about whether there are other instances of Reform aides having attempted to circumvent electoral law. It is likely to reopen intense scrutiny of Reform’s approach to donations and its finances, which are already the subject of a standards inquiry and police investigation.
In footage of another meeting, Jukes appeared to suggest to the fake UK-based supporter that his US-based father could make a substantial donation by channelling it through the son. When the possible structure was explained to Farage, footage of a meeting between him and the fake donors shows him saying: “Thank you both.”
At another point, Orr appeared to suggest that the fake UK-based donor and his US father might secure a meeting with Farage if he could promise a five- or six-figure sum – a meeting that later took place in Clacton over oysters and champagne.
In a different clip, Orr can be heard saying of the poll funding arrangement that Farage “doesn’t know, won’t know” and it was the kind of thing he would “rather not know”. At one point the footage shows him saying it was “totally legit” and with “nothing untowards about it at all”.
Jukes, a close aide to Farage, was also filmed meeting the fake donor, and at a Reform UK reception where in one conversation he appeared to introduce the undercover operative as a “key donor for off-the-book project”.
In footage of a meeting with the fake US donor, he is heard describing the polling as “clandestine” and “hugely important”.
The polling, conducted by JL Partners, made headlines before the local elections in May. The foreign source of funding and its links to Reform were not publicly disclosed. The Telegraph said it had suspended the articles about the polling, while the Times said it was not aware of the relationship with Reform.
After Channel 4 News’s broadcast, Bridget Phillipson, the Labour party chair, said the “scandal goes right to the top of Reform UK”. She added: “Nigel Farage needs to urgently prove today that his top team haven’t broken the law and secretly plotted to undermine our democracy.”
Ed Davey, the leader of the Liberal Democrats, called on the police and the Electoral Commission to investigate.

2 workers pulled alive from Nepal tunnel 9 days after disaster
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:10:00 UTC
16:10:00 KST

Two people were pulled alive from a tunnel Friday at a hydropower project on Nepal’s Trishuli River, nine days after an ice, rock and mudslide tore through the river valley, killing more than 1,200 people and displacing tens of thousands.
Officials and rescue workers believe the Aug. 26 collapse of a glacier in the upper reaches of the Trishuli River trapped at least 900 people inside tunnels serving six hydropower projects along the river.
At least 1,252 people were killed in Nepal after homes, roads and schools in towns and villages near the border with China’s Tibet region were swept away. More than 4,200 people remain missing, while thousands of others have been displaced.
China has reported 21 deaths in Tibet, with another 541 people listed as missing.
The two workers rescued Friday from a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station were the first people pulled alive from the hydropower projects. They were taken to an army hospital in the capital, Kathmandu, for treatment.
A small group of workers had managed to escape from another tunnel in the hours after the disaster struck, but no others had been rescued from the hydropower sites until Friday.
The workers rescued Friday were Sanjay Sah, a mechanical foreman, and Kabir Maharjan, a mechanical supervisor, the office of Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said in a statement.
Videos and photos released by Nepali authorities showed Maharjan being pulled out of a hole in the ground amid cheers from bystanders and placed on a stretcher.
Sah was carried on the back of a worker to a rescue tent, his face covered in mud.
In one video, a team of army doctors attended to Sah at a tent near the tunnel before he was taken to a hospital. They fitted what appeared to be an oxygen mask around his mouth and checked his vital signs.
“His name is Sanjay Sah and he was working in mechanical control room. The vital parameters look normal,” an army official said.
Sah told rescuers he spent time reciting mantras, or verses from a prayer, while he was trapped, according to The Kathmandu Post. He said three or four more people could be alive in the tunnel, and possibly more deeper inside.
Maharjan cannot move his hands and legs, while Sah’s injuries are not critical, an aide to the energy minister told Reuters.
Amir Maharjan, Kabir’s brother, said he had not received any official news but had been told to go to the hospital.
“I have been hearing from the news that my brother has been found. The entire family is very happy,” Amir said.
Both survivors were in the intensive care unit, a source at the army hospital where they were taken told Reuters, adding that their vital signs were stable.
A team of experts in a WhatsApp group was guiding rescue workers in the search at the hydropower projects, which has become a valuable tool alongside helicopters and heavy machinery in the race to find survivors.
More search and rescue operations were underway around the Upper Trishuli 3A project, the Nepali army said. Rescue efforts were being led by the army and police, with assistance from experts from India, South Korea and China.
Dhan Bahadur Tamang, who earlier escaped from a tunnel linked to the Upper Trishuli 1 hydropower project upriver from where the two men were pulled out Friday, said their rescue was a miracle and raised hopes of finding more survivors.
Property, housing and infrastructure worth at least 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees ($2.56 billion) were lost in last week’s catastrophe, Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, said Friday.
Nepal will need to rebuild around 20,000 houses in flood-ravaged areas, Upreti said Thursday, with at least 7,500 of those homes destroyed.
At least 583 foreign nationals were missing in the floods, Nepal said Thursday, many of them pilgrims and trekkers.
Australian disaster response specialists left for Nepal on Friday to join the search for survivors, as the government there expressed “serious concerns” about the welfare of its 36 missing citizens.

Philippines’ Duterte-Quiboloy ties on show at world’s largest arena launch
Though in custody on sex charges, Apollo Quiboloy still drew 80,000 followers and Duterte backing for his 75,000-seat Kingdome launch
3-MIN READ3-MIN
 Listen
The presence of former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte’s youngest son at the opening of detained televangelist Apollo Quiboloy’s 75,000-seat Kingdome stadium this week offered a striking display of how ties between the Duterte family and the Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KJC) have endured despite the criminal cases surrounding its founder.
Observers say the lavish inauguration, attended by an estimated 80,000 people alongside Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte, proved the organisation’s ability to maintain its political and institutional influence, even with its founder behind bars.
The event on Tuesday also featured an official city council tribute to Quiboloy and his church.
Quiboloy, who denies all allegations against him, remains in custody in the Philippines on charges of human trafficking and sexual abuse. Authorities are also reviewing a formal US request for his extradition.
Touted by local officials as a new architectural landmark, the Kingdome is now the world’s largest indoor arena, surpassing the 55,000-capacity Philippine Arena owned by another megachurch, the Iglesia ni Cristo (Church of Christ), in Bulacan province north of Manila.
The venue, where construction began in 2012, sits on the sprawling 30-hectare (2.15 million sq ft) KJC compound in Davao City. The site was the location of a 16-day police operation before the self-appointed “Son of God” pastor surrendered in September 2024. His legal counsel later called the surrender an “ultimate sacrifice” to avoid further “lawless violence” in the compound.
Quiboloy and eight associates were indicted by a US federal grand jury in 2021. He is wanted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation on charges of sex trafficking by force, fraud, coercion, sex trafficking of children, conspiracy and bulk cash smuggling. He is also accused of running a labour-trafficking scheme that forced church members on fraudulent visas to solicit donations for a non-existent charity.

Estonian Defence Minister resigns after being defrauded by Indian company
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:09:41 UTC
16:09:41 KST

Estonia’s Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned after a €70 million ($81.1 million) deal to buy artillery ammunition for Ukraine came under scrutiny over procurement failures.
Pevkur, who has served as defence minister since 2022, addressed the scandal while announcing his resignation on public broadcaster ETV on September 2.
“A leader must have the strength and courage to take responsibility,” Pevkur said in a Facebook post, adding that findings by the National Audit Office had raised questions over political responsibility.
The National Audit Office published a report on August 28 criticising defence procurements made by the Defence Ministry in recent years. The report warned that Estonia could ultimately have to cover the €70 million cost from its state budget.
According to Eesti Ekspress, an Estonian daily, Estonia signed the ammunition contract in 2024 with Datasel S.R.L., an Italian-registered company owned by Indian firm Neco Defense Munitions.
The contract was intended to supply artillery shells to Ukraine and was financed through the EU’s European Peace Facility.
Only some defective ammunition arrived
The Estonian Centre for Defence Investments (RKIK) made advance payments to Datasel, but shipments were repeatedly delayed and did not arrive for months.
A shipment eventually arrived in 2025, but Eesti Ekspress reported that the ammunition was defective and “useless”.
RKIK director-general Elmar Vaher, who oversaw the original contract, said the agreement should not have been signed because the supplier had no previous experience selling artillery shells.
“In my opinion, we should not have signed a contract with them,” Vaher said.
The deal was signed as Ukrainian forces faced severe ammunition shortages, worsened by delays in US military aid and the EU’s failure to meet its target of delivering one million rounds to Ukraine by March 2024.
The National Audit Office had repeatedly warned about risks surrounding defence spending, with its latest report raising concerns that the ammunition contract could ultimately burden Estonia’s budget.
Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal called a cabinet meeting for September 3 to discuss Pevkur’s resignation and the audit findings.
Estonia’s Prosecutor’s Office has also launched a criminal investigation into matters highlighted in the National Audit Office’s 2025 and 2026 reports.

Teen actor to play Bolt founder Markus Villig in upcoming movie
A feature film about the founding of Estonian startup Bolt is currently under production, with 16‑year‑old actor Tõru Kannimäe cast in the lead role as founder Markus Villig.
Villig founded Bolt, then known as Taxify, in 2013, when he was aged 19.
Kannimäe meanwhile has been keeping busy. He also stars in the youth film "Morten" premiering this weekend and the upcoming "Hõbevalge," based on the work by Lennart Meri, says playing a real person who is still alive presents a unique challenge.
"The filming isn't just taking place in summer, but will continue until next spring. It's quite a long process. But it's very different from the previous projects because this film is based on a true story, and I'm playing someone who actually exists and is alive. That's a major challenge," Kannimäe said.
Directed by Rain Rannu, the upcoming Villig biopic is currently using the working title "Taksoäpp" ("Taxi App"), and, the Tartu Film Fund says, tells the story of how a mobile app created by a young schoolboy grew into international tech unicorn Bolt.
As for Kannimäe, he began acting at the age of six in a drama group run by his mother. His breakthrough role came in "Fränk," another movie about youth in Estonia, which earned him an EFTA nomination for best actor this year. He had already been cast as the lead in "Morten" before his breakthrough in "Fränk."
The actor, who studies at Vanalinna Hariduskolleegium's theatre class, has worked with a range of directors of varying styles, including Tõnis Pill ("Fränk"), Ivan Pavljutškov ("Morten") and Martti Helde ("Hõbevalge"), as well as Rannu.
"Working with different directors has taught me a great deal. All the projects are very different and, as my mother emphasizes, that's the reality. Which is actually great, because you get to experience a lot of different things," Kannimäe said of this.
While last September the actor celebrated his 16th birthday on the set of "Hõbevalge," the Bolt project took up much of his summer this year and work is set to continue through to next spring.
The actor said his greatest passion remains film and theatre. "It has been my dream and goal for quite a long time, and I feel it is also my calling to act and do theatre and film — right now, that is my greatest passion," Kannimäe said.
Bolt is a mobility app platform which operates in over 50 countries worldwide and reported 2025 revenues of over €2 billion. It is one of nearly a dozen Estonian "unicorn" firms (valued at US$1 billion or more), with others including Wise, Pipedrive and Veriff.

Burkina Faso Conducts Target Practice With Most Weapons of Chinese Origin
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:07:54 UTC
16:07:54 KST

Burkina Faso Armed Forces conducted target practice using Chinese artillery and missile systems.
Footage of the Chinese weapons in action was broadcast by Burkina Faso’s national television.
During the exercises, the country also publicly demonstrated for the first time an air defense missile system not previously observed in its arsenal, which is likely the Sky Dragon 30.
The footage shows live-fire exercises involving CS/SH1 122 mm wheeled self-propelled howitzers, PLL-05 120 mm self-propelled mortars, and SR-5 modular multiple rocket launchers.
The CS/SH1 is a 122 mm artillery system mounted on a 6×6 wheeled chassis, with a claimed range of approximately 22–27 km, depending on the type of ammunition used. The PLL-05 self-propelled mortar is based on an armored vehicle from the WZ551 family and is equipped with a 120 mm gun-mortar. The military also deployed the SR-5 MLRS, capable of firing various types of guided and unguided rockets.
In the second half of the video, the deployment of the radar, operators working at the command post, and the launch of a SAM from a mobile launcher are shown.
According to Janes’ assessment, the dimensions of the launch pod containers are consistent with China’s Norinco Sky Dragon 30 system.
As for the specifications published by the manufacturer, the Sky Dragon 30 missile can engage aerial targets at ranges of up to 30 km and altitudes of up to 18 km. It is equipped with an infrared homing seeker, while the system is claimed to be capable of engaging up to 12 targets simultaneously.
The footage also shows a radar identified in open sources as the IBIS-150. The radar is reportedly capable of detecting aerial targets at ranges of up to 130 km and tracking up to 144 targets simultaneously.
The public demonstration of the Sky Dragon 30 marked the first known confirmation of the system’s presence in Burkina Faso. The country had not announced its procurement officially.
Burkina Faso’s military junta has received significant batches of Chinese-made armored vehicles since 2024.

BIRMINGHAM, England — Nigel Farage lost two of his closest advisers after they were caught in an undercover sting investigating party financing.
The start of the main day of the Reform UK conference in Birmingham on Friday was rocked by the resignations of Dan Jukes, Farage’s long-term media chief, and James Orr, his senior policy adviser.
The pair stepped down amid an internal party investigation after Channel 4 broadcast footage apparently showing them agreeing to take donations from a foreign benefactor via a middle-man in the U.K. Experts allege taking the cash and then seeking to hide its provenance could be a breach of U.K. electoral law.
Advertisement
Labour Party Chair Bridget Phillipson on Friday reported the matter to the Metropolitan Police, although no investigation has been launched by the force.
A Reform UK spokesman said: “Reform UK has launched an investigation following the broadcast of a Channel 4 News programme.
“Both individuals involved have stepped down from their respective positions pending the outcome of the investigation.
“The party believes it is important that the investigation is allowed to proceed independently and without prejudice. No further comment will be made while the investigation is ongoing.”
The departures mark an abrupt about-turn in Reform’s response to the Channel 4 sting. On Thursday night, the party went on the attack, claiming Jukes, Orr and Farage — who features in the footage — were “the target of a hoax perpetuated by foreign-funded, climate change activists” and denying any wrongdoing.
The footage broadcast by Channel 4 was gathered by Verbatim, an undercover reporting outfit linked to the Center for Climate Reporting.
Advertisement
The report showed Farage — who is due to give his main address at Reform’s Birmingham conference Friday afternoon following an appearance by French political ally Jordan Bardella — meeting undercover reporters posing as a wealthy U.S. backer and his son, and thanking the pair for their support. A U.S. citizen would not be a permissible donor under British electoral law.
Channel 4 News said the two men had at this point already funded £32,500-worth of polling commissioned by Reform, with the findings making their way into national newspapers with no declaration of the party’s involvement. This benefit in kind was not reported to watchdog the Electoral Commission.
Labour, which has been fighting to close a polling gap with Reform after a torrid two years in government, leapt on the Channel 4 report.
“We actually do have very tight rules around these things in this country for a reason, so that people have confidence in the electoral system and in our democracy,” Education Secretary Lucy Powell told Times Radio Friday morning. “But time and again, I think what we’re finding is Reform just think these rules don’t apply to them.”
Lee Anderson, Reform’s chairman, argued Friday that Farage himself has no further questions to answer on the affair, although admitted the row is a “distraction” as the party’s conference gets underway.
“The two people involved, they have gone. They have left the building,” he told Times Radio. “I keep saying this time and time again. They have gone. That is the right thing to do. They are not coming back and Nigel is going nowhere.”
Advertisement
He added: “Nigel is an honest man. I have known him for many years now. The party has done the right thing by launching this investigation. Nigel will be on the main stage later on explaining our first 100 days in government. He is not going anywhere.”
The stepping down of the two advisers is a significant blow to Farage. Orr is a British ally of U.S. Vice-President JD Vance and was appointed to the powerful role of head of policy just months ago. Jukes has served as a long-term media aide to Farage dating back to his days as leader of the Euroskeptic UK Independent Party.
This breaking story has been updated with additional developments. Clea Caulcutt contributed to the report.

Ukraine to Introduce Two-Level Air Raid Alert System as Drone Attacks Disrupt Daily Life
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:07:32 UTC
16:07:32 KST

Ukraine is overhauling its air raid alert system, introducing separate warning levels for drone and missile threats as relentless Russian drone attacks increasingly disrupt transportation, businesses and daily life.
Under the new system, a yellow alert will be used primarily for incoming Russian drones, while a red alert will signal missile threats, ballistic attacks and mass strikes, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced on Telegram on Thursday, Sept. 3.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The changes are designed to give businesses and the public more clarity over the level of danger while allowing parts of the economy to keep operating during less severe threats.
“Economy must keep working, taxes must continue flowing into the budget, and people must receive their salaries,” Koretskyi said.
“That is why businesses will be allowed to continue operating during a yellow-level alert, provided they strictly follow safety requirements.”
Businesses will be required to ensure employees and visitors have access to shelters. Companies without shelters will have three months to resolve the issue.
Kyiv to keep metro running during drone alerts
The government has recommended that Kyiv keep its metro operating normally during yellow-level alerts.
The capital should also increase surface public transportation when necessary, allowing people to reach workplaces, metro stations and hospitals despite ongoing drone threats.
Kyiv authorities have additionally been advised to shorten the current curfew to 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. The proposed changes would also allow transit heavy trucks and passenger transportation during curfew hours.
The government is also pushing communities to speed up the installation of additional mobile shelters to protect civilians from falling drone and missile debris.
The overhaul comes as Russia increasingly uses waves of drones to keep Ukraine under prolonged air threat, with attacks often stretching for hours rather than coming in a single strike.
In Kyiv, repeated alerts have already caused transport disruptions, while businesses have faced growing difficulties operating under the current all-or-nothing alert system.
The new two-tier approach is intended to allow the city and economy to function during drone threats while maintaining stricter restrictions when the risk escalates to missiles and mass attacks.

"What is the reason, or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?" he asked.

Swiss Patriot missile deal with Germany falls through
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:05:03 UTC
16:05:03 KST

Swiss Patriot missile deal with Germany falls through
Attempts by the Swiss army to order Patriot air missile systems via Germany have broken down, according to research by Swiss public broadcaster SRF.
The proposed German deal was set up to mitigate mounting delays and costs of ordering the systems directly from the United States.
The first Patriot air defence systems were supposed to arrive in Switzerland this year. However, last year the US abruptly allocated the delivery to Germany. This was because Germany had transferred its Patriot systems to Ukraine and wanted to quickly fill the gap.
In June the Federal Department of Defence saw an opportunity to enter into talks with Germany and the US. The ministry saw indications that Germany might at least cede parts of the delivery to Switzerland.
For example, Switzerland was encouraged by the fact that the Patriot systems did not correspond to the configuration ordered by Germany.
In recent weeks, the defence ministry was mandated by the government to negotiate with Germany as potential suppliers. However, these talks have now ended unsuccessfully. “The options with Germany have fallen through and cannot be implemented,” Urs Loher, director of defence procurement body Armasuisse, told SRF.
Loher does not blame Germany or the US. Given the threat level, everyone is looking out for themselves when it comes to defending against missiles. Germany has now chosen the fastest route. “Germany wants to replace the systems delivered to Ukraine as quickly as possible,” said Loher.
With the breakdown of negotiations, the Patriot air defense system will become even more expensive and will be delivered later. Had Switzerland reached an agreement with Germany, the additional costs would have amounted to “only” CHF1 billion.
Delivery would also have been possible from next year. Now, however, the additional costs are rising. Switzerland’s Patriot systems will now be built later than anticipated, so inflation will drive up the price tag. Minor upgrades are also costing more.
The additional costs now amount to at least CHF1.7 billion. And even this amount is not yet guaranteed. Loher speaks of additional costs of up to CHF4.3 billion. The original budget for the systems was CHF2 billion. Now, the best-case scenario forecasts at least a doubling of costs. In the worst case, they will triple.
The defence ministry now needs to reach an agreement with the US, either on an amendment to the existing contract or on a new one. “As long as the contracts are unsigned, nothing is certain,” said Loher.
Switzerland urgently needs the Patriot systems as the country is currently virtually unprotected missile attacks. However, the new situation delays delivery by at least six years until 2032. “We don’t expect it to be here before the early 2030s,” said Urs Loher.
In addition to Patriot, the government intends to purchase an additional long-range missile defense system. This purchase is likely to become even more urgent following the collapse of talks with Germany.
Negotiations are currently underway with potential suppliers from France, Israel, and South Korea. The planned expenditure is CHF5 billion. However, given the global security situation, it is uncertain how far this funding will stretch. Or how long it will take to receive air defence systems.

USS Lincoln crew hits the streets of Thailand's Pattaya after nine-month deployment
US sailors and Marines streamed into the Thai resort city of Pattaya Thursday after a record-breaking nine months at sea. Local police said there had so far been no major incidents connected to the 5,000-strong contingent of US service members, though two sailors were sent back to the ship after a drunken bar brawl.
Buses carrying crew members of the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier streamed into Thailand’s seaside resort city of Pattaya on Thursday, as part of a port call after a lengthy deployment to the Middle East.
Read moreUSS Lincoln carrier docks near Thailand's Pattaya resort after nine months at sea
The Lincoln was supporting the US-Israeli war against Iran, and its deployment included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea of more than 260 days. Its lengthy deployment drew concerns last month about deteriorating mental health among the crew, including reported attempted suicides, as well as shortages of key food supplies aboard.
The Navy downplayed any problems, and US President Donald Trump maintained that the deployment was “not nearly long enough”.
The ship has been deployed for a total of 286 days, according to the US Embassy in Bangkok. Its total uninterrupted time at sea before Wednesday’s arrival in Chonburi province was 264 days.
The ship is expected to depart Thailand this weekend and continue its journey back to the US.
Pattaya draws in huge crowds of foreign tourists, both for its beach resorts and its nightlife. The seaside city has come under heavy scrutiny for its widespread sex tourism industry.
Thai authorities launched a crackdown on sex workers ahead of the ship's visit, although they denied it was linked to the sailors' arrival.
Shore leave
After clambering down from buses, laden with luggage, several service members told the Associated Press they were excited to be in Thailand.
Vendors and travel agents gathered outside the Hard Rock Hotel, the designated pickup and drop-off point for troops travelling from the Lincoln, which is docked nearby at Laem Chabang port.
They swarmed service members as they arrived, offering a range of souvenirs and services. Many sailors waved them away while waiting for their rides.
Two other ships from the Lincoln’s strike group are docked elsewhere in Thailand, with the destroyer USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. at Chonburi’s Sriracha port and the cruiser USS Robert Smalls in Map Ta Phut in neighbouring Rayong province.
A-ngoon Sombat travelled 200 kilometres between Pattaya and the central province of Ayutthaya to sell colourful braided bracelets to the visiting crew, as she does every time she hears a US ship is coming for a port call in Chonburi province.
She set up opposite the hotel entrance and had managed to make some sales, but said she is still unsure if business will be good this week.
“There are many vendors around. It’s really up to how lucky each of us are,” she said.
Dozens of service members could be spotted strolling around Pattaya's Terminal 21 mall with shopping bags in their hands as the afternoon sun was blazing outside.
A 20-year-old serving as a navigator aboard the Petersen, who declined to give his name because he was told not to speak to media while ashore, said the morale among his crew members was really high now that they had arrived in Thailand.
The sailor said it was his first deployment for the US Navy. He said it was a bit of an ordeal but he was happy to finally be on his way home.
He declined to comment when asked about the reports about the conditions on the Lincoln.
Other service members seem to have been less restrained.
Two sailors were sent back to the ship after a drunken altercation, Thai police said Friday.
Police were alerted to a "small scuffle" involving the sailors in the early hours of Thursday near Pattaya's nightlife hotspot Walking Street, city police chief Colonel Anek Srathongyoo told AFP.
"The sailors were drunk and they were fighting, making loud noise," he said.
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
He described the incident as "trivial" and said local residents had only called police to prevent it from escalating.
The unidentified sailors were not charged as "they did not violate any Thai law", Anek said.
The US Navy sent the pair back to the ship, he added.
The police chief said there had been no other notable incidents since the Lincoln docked, and one Pattaya masseuse said it had been calmer than previous military port calls.
'Engineering marvel'
A spot just outside the Laem Chabang port had turned into a small attraction by Wednesday evening, as people gathered to catch a glimpse of the Lincoln.
People arrived by car and motorcycle to peer through a mesh fence at the ship, which is as long as about three American football fields. They took photos and videos, excitedly chatted with strangers about their chance to see the vessel.
American Keith Eldridge, who has lived in Thailand for five years, travelled from the neighbouring province of Chachoengsao just to see the ship. He was too late to catch the Lincoln docking but found the viewing spot through a recommendation from other enthusiasts he met along the way.
He said it was impressive for him to get to lay his eyes on this “engineering marvel”.
“When you get to look at something so big, wrapped up with so much technology, the radars, the sonars, the weapon systems, the propulsion systems, it is truly amazing that we can build it, float it, and we fight from it,” he said.
The Lincoln’s commanding officer, Captain Dan Keeler, said the ship will be heading home soon, but may make further supply stops. He declined to comment on the exact date the strike group is expected back in the US.
(FRANCE 24 with AP and AFP)

Russia shifts tactics with round-the-clock air strikes on Kyiv, disrupting daily life
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:01:44 UTC
16:01:44 KST

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Thursday night he hoped to host US President Donald Trump's envoys in Kyiv in the coming days to resume efforts to end the war.
For much of the war, Russian drone and missile attacks on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv followed a particular rhythm; they almost always came at night.
The warnings would begin on monitoring channels on Telegram in the late evening. They announced drones moving south, missiles being launched, air defences working.
Ukrainian civilians judged whether it was prudent to stay indoors or make for shelter in the metro based on the severity of the threat.
Now, Russia has changed tactics with the use of fast-flying, jet-powered drones and the expectation that daylight brings a return to normal life has been shattered.
Since last week, attacks have come day and night, compounding the terror of overnight strikes with the exhaustion of constant daytime disruption.
In Kyiv, the recurring wail of air-raid sirens has become part of daily life. It has interrupted commutes, shopping trips and children’s schools, intruded on life’s biggest moments, from weddings to funerals, and, as these attacks always have, taken lives.
The relentless alerts are exhausting residents, leaving some wondering how long they can stay.
Part of daily life
An alert sounds. People look at their phones or up at the sky. Moments later, in the distance, the familiar sounds of air defences intercepting drones resound.
Plumes of smoke can often be seen rising in the distance. Photos quickly spread across Telegram channels, showing where the destruction has occurred.
An hour or two later, another siren echoes.
In malls, banks and other businesses, air-raid protocols require customers and staff to leave when an alert sounds. A bank transaction can be interrupted mid-conversation; a shopping trip can become a cycle of entering a store, evacuating, returning and evacuating again.
Getting the shopping done has become a nightmare for Volodymyr Bovsunovskyi, who recounts a recent family trip to a mall to buy clothes for his nearly 4-year-old daughter.
They had been inside for about 20 minutes when the alert sounded. They rushed out and saw smoke rising nearby. They never got to purchase the clothes.
“A lot has changed in the last seven days,” he said. Like many residents, he hopes the attacks will relent. But, they have not yet, as Ukraine struggles to find an effective way to counter them.
Train journeys that would normally take a few hours have stretched much longer. In some cases, passengers have found themselves walking for hours through grassy fields after trains stopped on the tracks, carrying their belongings while one air-raid alert followed another.
The same uncertainty extends to getting around the city.
When GPS signals are disrupted to jam drones, using a taxi app becomes a difficult process. A car that appears to be nearby can suddenly appear to be on the other side of the world.
A pickup that seemed imminent suddenly shows an arrival time of thousands of minutes.
Considering leaving
Ivan Datsiv, an IT worker, was in his apartment in Kyiv’s Podil district when a Russian drone tore through the floor on Tuesday, charring the ceilings and walls and completely destroying the flat next door.
Datsiv tries to joke about it, saying he had been meaning to repaint the walls anyway.
The alerts have become so frequent that he no longer sees the point of repeatedly going to a shelter. At this rate, he said, the only alternative would be to live in the basement.
“The alarms sound constantly,” he said. “You don’t even have time to go down and come back up. It’s just a waste of time running back and forth."
He is thinking of leaving Kyiv. “I’m thinking of living in another city, somewhere quiet and without this danger,” he said.
From the blown-out apartment next door, the view looks down onto a playground and basketball court where children are still playing.
Then a siren sounds again. Minutes later, the white zigzagging trail of an intercepted drone can be seen against the sky.
Bovsunovskyi is also considering leaving the city for a while, hoping to give his family, including his pregnant wife, a chance to rest.
The kindergarten his daughter attends must move the children to a shelter whenever an air-raid alert sounds. The alerts have become so frequent that he now simply picks her up halfway through the day.
“There is no stability,” he said.
Ending the war
Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Thursday night he hoped to host US President Donald Trump's envoys in Kyiv in the coming days to resume efforts to end the war.
Diplomatic push to end Russia's four-and-a-half-year invasion has stalled in recent months as the United States has shifted its focus towards the war with Iran.
"We expect to see the envoys of the President of America here in Kyiv. We have confirmation from them," Zelensky said in his nightly address.
"They will have meetings in Moscow and in Kyiv. We are counting on a meeting in the coming days," he added.
Trump's special envoys, Steve Witkoff and the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner, have been involved in shuttle diplomacy between Russia and Ukraine, travelling to Moscow multiple times.
They have never been to Kyiv.
Zelenskyy said that "tentative dates have been set" for the envoys' first visit to the Ukrainian capital, which has endured intensified Russian drone and missile attacks over the past week.
Russia's invasion of Ukraine has turned into Europe's worst conflict since World War II, killing thousands of civilians and hundreds of thousands of troops.

First in the Baltics: Northway Biotech opens €61 million cell therapy and personalized medicine CDMO in Vilnius
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:01:25 UTC
16:01:25 KST

Building on more than 22 years of CDMO experience across biologics and advanced therapies, Northway Biotech is significantly expanding its development and manufacturing capacity with a new 3,500 sq. m facility featuring up to 20 independent cGMP manufacturing lines and first customer programs already secured.
The first dedicated Innovative Cell Therapy and Personalized Medicine Center of its kind in the Baltic States has opened in Vilnius, Lithuania, marking a major expansion of Northway Biotech’s CDMO capabilities in advanced therapies. The Northway Group has invested €61 million in the new 3,500 sq. m facility within the broader BIO CITY III development.
The center significantly expands Northway Biotech’s established CDMO platform across mammalian and microbial biologics, gene therapy, and cell-based technologies, adding substantial new development and cGMP manufacturing capacity for advanced and personalized therapies. It will support biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, university hospitals, and research institutions and begins operations with its first customers already on board and contracts in place.
The facility brings together specialized infrastructure and technologies for the development and cGMP manufacturing of autologous and allogeneic cell-based therapies, personalized therapeutic vaccines, regenerative medicine applications, and 3D human tissue technologies. Its segregated manufacturing infrastructure enables multiple cell-based products and processes to be handled in parallel while maintaining stringent requirements for product identity, quality, traceability, and contamination control.
A €61 million investment scaling 15 years of specialized expertise
The opening also marks a significant milestone for Kamieninių ląstelių tyrimų centras (Stem Cell Research Center), the company operating the new facility under the Northway Biotech brand, which celebrates its 15th anniversary this year. Founded in 2011 by Prof. Vladas Algirdas Bumelis, the company has spent 15 years building practical experience in cGMP environments and systematically developing its expertise in stem cell research, cell-based technologies, and advanced therapeutic applications.
“Fifteen years ago, we did not have a €61 million center – we had people and ambition. Over the years, we have built practical experience, grown our team, and advanced our cell technology capabilities. Today, we are systematically taking all of this to an entirely new scale. What seemed like the future of medicine 15 years ago is now being created here in Lithuania,” says Prof. Vladas Algirdas Bumelis, founder of the Northway Group.
The significance of the center for Lithuania is also highlighted by the President of the Republic of Lithuania, Gitanas Nausėda.
“This center is about people. About scientists who will be able to stay in Lithuania and work with technologies that are shaping the future of medicine. About patients for whom personalized medicine is not an abstract concept, but a real treatment option. And about all of us as a country, proving that we can be not only observers, but creators at the global frontier of science,” says President Gitanas Nausėda.
Up to 20 manufacturing lines for advanced and personalized therapies
The new center will operate up to 20 independent cGMP-compliant manufacturing lines. It features quality control laboratories, advanced cleanroom systems, and segregated infrastructure designed for the manufacturing of highly sensitive cell therapies.
In personalized therapies, an individual manufacturing process may be dedicated to a single patient – their cells and their disease.
“We are accustomed to traditional pharmaceutical manufacturing, where a single process produces medicines for large numbers of patients. Here, in some cases, an entire manufacturing process may be dedicated to just one person. It is a completely different pharmaceutical model – and this is precisely the kind of medicine this center was built for,” says Prof. Bumelis.
The center’s services are targeted at international biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, university hospitals, and research centers. With first customers already on board, Northway Biotech will provide development and manufacturing services for advanced therapies from the new Vilnius facility.
From cancer-targeting cells to longevity medicine
The new facility will enable Northway Biotech to significantly scale up its capabilities in cell and tissue technologies.
One area involves technologies in which a patient’s immune cells are modified to enable them to recognize and destroy specific cancer cells. In parallel, 3D human tissue technologies are being developed to create more physiologically relevant tissue models, study drug effects, and advance regenerative medicine solutions.
Northway’s expertise in cell biology and tissue engineering will also be further applied to regenerative medicine, including research into the mechanisms of tissue regeneration and ways to preserve or restore tissue function. The development of personalized therapeutic vaccine technologies will also continue on a larger scale.
A €61 million step toward the 5% of GDP target
Northway’s investment contributes to Lithuania’s ambition for the life sciences sector to account for 5% of the country’s GDP by 2030.
The new center is expected to bring together approximately 100 life sciences professionals. The €61 million investment project is financed through private funds and a loan from Lithuania’s national development bank ILTE under the Milijardas verslui (Billion for Business) initiative.
“Today, Lithuania is not only a user of advanced technologies, but also a country where they are created and developed. The opening of the BIO CITY center is an important step in strengthening Lithuania’s biomedical ecosystem and our position in the international market. We have a strong foundation for the sector’s continued growth – Lithuania is home to highly qualified professionals in biomedicine, medicine, and science, while growing investment demonstrates international confidence in our potential,” says Edvinas Grikšas, Minister of the Economy and Innovation.
The new center becomes another part of the BIO CITY ecosystem being developed by Northway.
BIO CITY I brings together Northway Biotech’s mammalian and microbial biologics development and manufacturing capabilities across Vilnius and Boston, while BIO CITY II is home to the gene therapy center. BIO CITY III now significantly expands capacity in cell therapy and personalized medicine, further strengthening Northway Biotech’s integrated CDMO platform across biologics and advanced therapies.
ABOUT THE NORTHWAY GROUP
The Northway Group comprises 17 companies with more than 20 years of experience across biotechnology, biopharmaceuticals, private medicine, wellness, and investment.
Its biotechnology cluster, operating under the Northway Biotech brand, consists of seven companies: five in Lithuania, one in the United Kingdom, and one in the United States. The biotechnology companies employ more than 200 highly qualified professionals, while Northway works with more than 100 partners worldwide, including pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, research institutions, and universities. Its key export markets are Europe, North America, and Asia.
Northway Biotech is a member of the Lithuanian consortium for cooperation with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). In recognition of its leadership in biologics development and manufacturing, the company received an Outsourced Pharma 2025 CDMO Leadership Award in the global biologics CDMO category.
Source: northwaybiotech.com

Earle Meets World Is One Long ‘Get Ready With Me’ Video
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:01:03 UTC
16:01:03 KST

“You’re gonna see everything on this show,” Alix Earle assures viewers in the voiceover that opens her Netflix reality series Earle Meets World. But if the show made a genuine effort to fulfill the 25-year-old social media star’s vow to reveal the rawest, most intimate aspects of her life, then the only reasonable conclusion to draw from it would be that there just isn’t much to see.
As her fans (she has 8.5 million on TikTok alone) will anticipate, “everything” refers specifically to ongoing drama around Earle’s parents’ divorce, her own breakup with NFL player Braxton Berrios, and her mysterious falling-out with fellow creator and former boss Alex Cooper. All of this does indeed come up in the eight-episode series, now streaming in full, which tries mightily to position the large, blended Earle family as the Kardashian-Jenners for a new generation. Yet the bombshells teased in months’ worth of promotional materials aren’t especially explosive. Nor is there a breakout personality among a cast that, understandably enough, seems either too chill or too concerned with appearing likable to really entertain. Earle Meets World plays less like a juicy docusoap than like a tediously extended version of the Get Ready With Me (GRWM) videos that made its subject famous—one that suggests less overlap than you might expect between the qualities of a successful influencer and those required for reality TV stardom.
Earle is one of those celebrities who are universally known to people under 30 but barely on the radar of anyone much older. (I’ll admit to having confused her with Cooper, another all-American blonde who parlayed internet fame into a Netflix series, and I know I’m not the only one.) Though I wouldn’t recommend making the show your first trip down the Alix Earle rabbit hole, here is a quick intro for the unfamiliar: Conventionally beautiful yet plagued by cystic acne, Earle grew her following as a University of Miami undergrad with mirror-facing GRWM TikToks, eventually going viral with a vulnerable post about her skin troubles. Then came the brand deals and new platforms. Cooper signed Earle, an obvious heir, to her podcast network; they abruptly parted ways in early 2025 and have been vaguely but publicly feuding ever since. Meanwhile, Earle has continued her ascent, launching a skincare brand, Reale Actives, and introducing herself to people elderly enough to watch network TV on Dancing With the Stars.
Synergistically positioned to bring her social media followers to a streaming platform that needs young subscribers to maintain its dominance while filling gaps in her own reach, Earle Meets World is a multigenerational family soap. Alix and 23-year-old Ashtin—a less-extroverted brunette whose TikTok audience still tops a million—are the It-girl sisters who constantly squabble but consider each other best friends. Their mom, Alisa, and dad, TJ, have been divorced for more than a decade, their split catalyzed by TJ’s affair with Ashley Dupré, a key character in the prostitution scandal that sank former New York governor Eliot Spitzer. Now Dupré is Ashley Earle, TJ’s wife and the mother of their three kids; the eldest, Izabel, is, at 13, already cranking out Outfit of the Day videos like the Gen Alpha Kylie Jenner she has the pedigree to become. A recent breast cancer survivor, Alisa has her own longtime partner, Todd. Her messy separation from TJ has evidently given way to a tenuous friendship between the couples, although it seems doubtful they spend as much time together off-camera as on. These relationships are further complicated by the role TJ, who made his fortune in construction, has assumed as Alix and Ashtin’s “dadager.”
All the raw material for an unscripted family drama is present. Somehow, though, the fireworks tend to fizzle as soon as they’re lit. With the divorce so far in the past, a season’s worth of halfhearted conflict among the parents is wrung out of TJ joking that Alisa could be a “young piece of ass” on The Golden Bachelor. Ashley’s friction with Alix is framed as fallout from the latter’s history of oversharing about the former but feels more like standard stepfamily tension, heightened by reality-TV producers' prodding and Alix’s hypervigilance about her stepmom’s sometimes-awkward social media presence. Ironically, we only really witness the self-centered, control-freak behavior relatives are always attributing to Alix when she’s struggling to manage her image and brand identity. As a result, the most intense moments of the series tend to involve cringey TikToks or premature glimpses of Reale Actives packaging. You probably have to be a diehard Earle girl to find this stuff compelling. And even if you are, you might be disappointed by how many climactic Earle Meets World scenes, from Ashtin kicking Alix out of her New York apartment to Cooper goading Alix to come at her, unfold in now-ancient vertical videos that already have millions of views.
It doesn’t help the show that the two people with whom Alix seems most preoccupied throughout the season—Cooper and Berrios—aren’t present. Instead, we get her side of these stories, conveyed in interviews and stiff conversations over cocktails at trendy, jewel-toned lounges, often so stripped of details that they come off as, respectively, a generic exploitative mentorship and your typical ambivalent breakup. A scene in the premiere that seems even more staged than the average docusoap grievance dump has Alix talking with TJ about Cooper in sentences that could’ve been scripted by a crisis-PR pro: “I definitely feel betrayed by Alex Cooper.” “She took advantage of my admiration for her.” Neither this storyline nor the Berrios one advances until the very end of the season, and even those late developments are anticlimactic. (Tabloid headlines linking Earle and Tom Brady, meanwhile, get coy winks but no substantive context.)
Much of the blame for Earle Meets World’s slightness and superficiality, as well as the shapelessness of episodes that drag despite running less than 40 minutes apiece, should fall on the show’s producers. Not only have they failed to identify entertaining narratives within this family’s daily life; they’ve also made their desperation to do so too apparent in the final product. To be fair, they had a difficult assignment. As eager as they look to be on screen together, the Earles are—or act—too calm and conciliatory to drive reality-soap plots. No one wants to look unhinged, least of all Alix, who talks about being unstable but can’t risk her credibility as an entrepreneur, pitchwoman, and parasocial companion to millions by getting truly ugly on camera. Which is precisely what natural born reality stars have always done. Compare Alix and Ashtin’s nights at the club to the sloppy-drunk violence and infidelity of the 20-somethings on Jersey Shore and Vanderpump Rules, or her parents’ relationships to chaotic Real Housewives marriages, and it all looks rather tame. No one here can quip like the best Bravo scrappers and Traitors debaters, either, so the show lacks the element of humor that suffuses every classic of the genre.
Influencers fall into a cultural gray area between entertainment and entrepreneurship; most excel at one more than the other. Both fields demand storytelling skills. But that doesn’t mean a person with a preternatural ability to sell people the products they watch her apply to her face as she scatters breadcrumbs about her personal life necessarily has the makings of an unscripted drama’s protagonist. Earle might be too shrewd a businesswoman to have unadulterated main character energy.

Russia attacks Ukraine with missile and 121 drones: 103 UAVs shot down or jammed
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
10:01:00 EEST
16:01:00 KST

Russia attacks Ukraine with missile and 121 drones: 103 UAVs shot down or jammed
Russian forces have attacked Ukraine with a Kh-31P air-launched missile and 121 drones of various types since the evening of 3 September. Ukrainian forces have downed 103 of the drones, while strikes have been recorded at a number of locations.
Source: Ukrainian Air Force
Quote: "As of 09:30, air defence systems had shot down or jammed 103 Russian Shahed- and Gerbera-type drones, UAVs of other types and S8000 Banderol drones in the north, south, east and centre of the country. Strikes by Russian aerial weapons have been recorded at 15 locations, and downed debris has landed at six locations."
Details: Russian forces launched the missile from the Black Sea, while the drones were launched from the direction of the Russian cities of Millerovo, Oryol and Kursk as well as from temporarily occupied Donetsk and Hvardiyske in occupied Crimea.
The aerial attack has been repelled by aircraft, anti-aircraft missile forces, electronic warfare assets, unmanned systems units and mobile fire groups from Ukraine's defence forces.
As of the morning of 4 September, the attack is ongoing, as several Russian drones are still in Ukrainian airspace.

Russia attacked Ukraine with missile and drones with "Banderols" from different directions - how air defense performed
Kyiv • UNN
At night, Russia launched an Kh-31P missile and 121 drones at Ukraine. Air defense shot down or suppressed 103 unmanned aerial vehicles; hits were recorded at 15 locations.
Russia launched a missile and 121 drones at Ukraine during the night of September 4, 103 of which were shot down or suppressed. UNN reports this, citing data from the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
With what and from where the Russians attacked
According to the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, during the night of September 4 (from 18:00 on September 3), the enemy attacked with:
-  a Kh-31P guided air-launched missile from the Black Sea, as well as 121 Shahed-type attack UAVs (about half of them jet-powered), Gerbera drones, Parodiya-type decoy drones, and S8000 "Banderol" drones; 
-  from the following directions: Millerovo, Oryol, Kursk, the temporarily occupied territory of Donetsk region, and Hvardiiske – the temporarily occupied territory of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea. 
How many were shot down and where
The air attack was repelled by aviation, anti-aircraft missile troops, electronic warfare and unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups of Ukraine’s Defense Forces.
According to preliminary data, as of 09:30, air defense forces had shot down/suppressed 103 enemy Shahed-type UAVs, Gerbera drones, drones of other types, and S8000 "Banderol" drones in the north, south, east, and center of the country
Were there any hits
Hits by enemy air-attack weapons were recorded at 15 locations, as well as the fall of downed targets (debris) at 6 locations.
The attack is ongoing; enemy UAVs remain in the airspace.

Another Chinese EV maker joins grid in Europe, with Xiaomi to launch sales next year
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:00:10 UTC
16:00:10 KST

Another Chinese EV maker joins grid in Europe, with Xiaomi to launch sales next year
Xiaomi Auto says it has signed agreements with eight car dealer groups to build a sales and service network in Germany
Chinese tech firm Xiaomi will start selling electric cars in Europe next year, it announced at a consumer electronics trade show in Berlin on Thursday, adding to the growing list of Chinese carmakers expanding into the European market despite EU tariffs on China-made electric vehicles (EVs) and growing wariness across the bloc.
Xiaomi Auto, the group’s EV arm, said it would enter several European markets including Germany, where it had signed agreements with eight car dealer groups to build a sales and service network ahead of the launch.
The immediate obstacle would be Brussels’ countervailing duties on Chinese EVs. Since Xiaomi did not participate in an EU anti-subsidy investigation launched in 2023 – it only launched its first EV in China in March 2024 – it is likely to be hit with the highest duty of 35.3 per cent on the cars it exports to the EU, on top of the standard 10 per cent import duty.
Xiaomi declined to comment on whether it was in discussions with the European Commission on a price undertaking offer that would spare it the levy.
At the launch event at IFA Berlin, Xiaomi executives struck a positive tone on its expansion to Europe.
“Xiaomi Auto is committed to long-term investment in Europe,” said Yu Liguo, vice-president of Xiaomi Auto and head of its international business. Alongside its research and development centre in Munich, he said partnerships with local dealers would be key to its European expansion.

Breaking Down the Stunning Finale of Silo Season 3
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
07:00:00 UTC
16:00:00 KST

Following the stunning final scene of Season 2 of Silo, the third season has diverged into two timelines: one with Juliette (Rebecca Ferguson) and company in Silo 18 fighting for their survival, and another unfolding before the silo program began.
The season’s penultimate episode delivered some big revelations: The all-knowing Algorithm program that ensures the survival of the silo isn’t actually a digital algorithm, but a person watching from Silo 1, deciding everyone’s fates. Before he dies in Episode 9, Bernard (Tim Robbins) offers some hope: “A person can be defeated.” Meanwhile, in the past timeline, Daniel (Ashley Zukerman) and Helen (Jessica Henwick) discover the origins of the silos, only for a shocking nuclear explosion to separate them.
That’s a hell of a way to end an episode, and the Season 3 finale of Silo, “Troy,” brings us straight into Silo 1, where those running the system live, far in the future. How far, exactly? “Three hundred and fifty years,” says series creator Graham Yost. “It’s revealed in Episode 9 that the silos were part of a 500-year plan. And they're 350 years into that.”
A memory suppression system
Inside Silo 1, we see Daniel waking from cryo-sleep. Except he’s no longer called Daniel: He is now Troy. And while Troy looks physically the same as Daniel, he’s completely changed. That’s made crystal clear when he settles into his shift and has to deal with the outbreak in Silo 17, the same silo Juliette ventured to in Season 2. Troy, without hesitation, delivers a ruthless decision to execute every single person—man, woman, and child—who left the silo. A top priority of Silo 1 is to prevent silos from discovering that any other silos exist. His decision to unleash drone warfare is met with disapproval by drone pilot Susan, who is actually Daniel’s sister Charlotte (Jessica Brown Findlay). Neither of them recognizes one another from the past. “He’s completely bloodless about it. Totally unemotional. It’s just his job,” says Yost. (Yost does suggest that Charlotte’s negative reaction to Troy’s behavior is worth our attention, though he won’t say why).
That lack of emotion bears no resemblance to the past Daniel. It turns out there’s a system designed to keep memories suppressed. Yost divulges some key details behind this Silo 1 initiative. “Your skill set, your skill knowledge, your expertise stays with you, and so that's why Daniel, as an engineer, is someone who can solve problems. There is an effort to wipe and control memory, so people don't know who they were. But they know who they became in the project.” Yost says we’ll discover more about specifics next season.
It’s precisely the same idea the Algorithm pushed Camille to implement in Silo 18, a major plot point of Season 3. If she had done it, the silo would have continued to function, but there would have been huge problems. “People would forget they had kids and not feed them, and people would forget they were married to each other,” says Yost. The memory suppression plotline is influenced by a book by British neurologist Oliver Sacks. “In one of his books, a guy has extraordinary short-term memory loss. He’ll say ‘Hello, nice to meet you’ every 15 seconds or so. But if he sits down at the piano, he can play an entire concerto. So there's something about that persistence of memory; that part of his brain keeps going. We modeled it on that.”
The person behind the Algorithm
We also discover that Daniel reports to Victor (Matt Craven), whom audiences first met as Charlotte’s doctor at the beginning of the season and who is one of the leading minds behind the silo program. Further, we see that Victor is actually the voice behind the almighty Algorithm. Victor seems deeply disturbed by Troy’s willingness to massacre the people of silo. Interestingly, he does not have a different name from the one he had before—and neither does the silo director, Senator Rosalind Thurman (Laura Innes). They have maintained their identities, and unlike Daniel/Troy, they know everything that’s happened in the last 350 years. “Power dictates who is in power, and that power gets to retain memory. But there’s a burden in retaining memory,” Yost says.
Troy comes to Victor with a request. He’s pestered by visions of a woman, who we know is Helen. These flashbacks play on his mind, and he hopes that Victor can help him find out who she is. “The whole purpose and design of the project is to free us from the past,” Victor tells Troy, gently brushing off his request. Victor makes a note of it before Troy goes back to cryo-sleep until his next shift. It’s revealed that Troy has been asking Victor for information about Helen ever since he became part of the silo over 300 years ago, as we see a folder full of the times he’s asked about her.
With Troy back in cryo-sleep, some time later, Victor has a new problem to deal with: the uprising in Silo 18. Victor has put the dreaded safeguard in motion, a fail-safe created by the silo founders to annihilate an entire silo’s population if rebellion or a discovery of knowledge threatens the entirety of the silo system. Camille (Alexandria Riley), Silo 18’s head of IT, now armed with the knowledge that the Algorithm is human, manages to outsmart it, providing a distraction to stop the safeguard by capping the concealed pipe that would flood the silo with lethal poison gas.
It’s a monumental success for Silo 18, and a crushing blow for Silo 1, one that could threaten to destroy the entire system and everything that’s been building for over 300 years. And yet, Victor’s face does not register the disappointment we might expect. “He felt relieved that Silo 18 didn’t die,” says Yost.
It’s a surprise, but given what follows, it makes plenty of sense. Victor ends up taking his own life. “We never land on exactly why he killed himself, but there are a lot of different reasons, says Yost. “It's a constellation, more than one trigger. But I think that for him, a big trigger was seeing Daniel, this guy that he quite liked, do this horrific thing. It's like, ‘Is that what we are? Is that what we've done?’ I think when he realized he was actually happy that 18 survived, he knew he wasn't on board with this anymore.”
Juliette’s plan for Silo 1
Thirty-five years later, Troy is awoken from cryo-sleep again, and learns that Victor is no longer alive. Troy is to take over as the Algorithm, and faces off against Juliette, who’s approached the giant door at the bottom of the Silo 18. In Silo 18, that door is referred to as “the forward vault,” suggesting that the door is actually a path to another silo. This means that the massacre of Silo 17 happened approximately 35 years before we met Juliette for the first time in Silo Season 1.
As Juliette and friends approach the door, the Algorithm (a.k.a. Troy) communicates with them. They strike a deal. If Juliette agrees to stop investigating, Silo 1 won’t attempt any further safeguarding, leaving them in peace. Juliette accepts the offer, but she doesn’t mean it. Troy threatened to kill everyone in the silo should Juliette not agree, and she believes it’s only a matter of time before they try and kill everyone again.
Juliette has the genesis of a plan. “They’re expecting us to defend ourselves, which means they won’t be preparing to defend against us. If we can get to them first, we can protect everyone. We need to take out Silo 1” she declares. 
Before the season ends, Troy finds an encrypted message from Victor. The message threatens to undo 350 years of memory wiping: “Her name is Helen Drew,” Victor reveals to Troy. We close in on Troy’s face as tears fall down his cheeks as he says Helen’s name out loud, and the episode cuts to black.
Hints for what’s to come in Season 4
“The big things we wanted to set up at the end of the season were Juliette saying we have to take down Silo 1, and Daniel saying Helen’s name,” says Yost. These events seem to set up a Season 4 battle between Troy and Juliette, one that could topple the entire silo system. But Troy’s realization seems to suggest that he may in fact revert to Daniel, which could mean that he will instead begin to work against Silo 1, opening a possibility of teaming up with Juliette to take the silos down for good.
Yost, of course, will not reveal if this, or anything like it, will happen in Season 4, the final season of Silo, currently scheduled for sometime next summer. But there is one thing Yost will say about the upcoming struggle between Silo 1 and Silo 18:
“This is war.”
